title: Content-bound completion and release readback
outcomes: A current opted-in task can complete only after its declared checks, review, requirements and release are proven for the delivered content.

in: Typed local verification capture, critic evidence, declared release readback and one completion gate across finish/approval/reporting
out: Automatic version/tag/publish orchestration and deployment adapters; those remain abc-06/07
boundaries: Canonical task proof, local Git content and read-only release provider verification

decision_rights: Authorize execution and choose model; GO on 2026-09-13
Implement bounded contract choices and document compatibility behavior

constraints: Opt-in execution contracts require strict completion evidence on every current finish/approval path; preserve historical done records and unconfigured legacy semantics under abc-d01.
Run declared local verification commands and retain exact task/revision/content/cwd/exit/raw-evidence binding. Empty prose or copied stale success is insufficient.
Separate work/review/release state; a failed required push or unknown publisher cannot become done or completed_tasks.
Verify explicit remote branch/tag/publication identity for the final product content; operational .go evidence writes are distinguished from material source/config changes.
Support read-only Git-tag and GitHub-release proof; do not perform publication or infer deployment. Unknown release profiles fail closed.
Keep all task and campaign reporting honest when another open/active/blocked task remains.

quality_attributes.scenario: Failed/missing shipping proof through any finish/approval route
Code or verification evidence changes after green
quality_attributes.measure: Stale proof accepted for delivered content

quality_attributes.scenario: Empty, failed, forged-shape or unrelated command evidence
quality_attributes.measure: Mandatory checks bypassed by field presence

risks: Local evidence hashes establish consistency and provenance within the trusted controller boundary; they are not cryptographic attestation of a model or an independent reviewer.
